findings.evidence: `CauchyPrincipalValue.lean` exposes `cauchyPVAt`, `HasCauchyPVAt.cauchyPVAt_eq`, `.unique`, `.congr_along_curve`, `.zero`, `.const_mul`, `.add`, `.sum`, and `CauchyPVExistsAt.*` at lines 109, 154, 159, 174, 185, 199, 216, 234, 288, 296, 304, 310; the new file only defines `HasCauchyPV`, `hasCauchyPV_iff`, `.intro`, `CauchyPVExists`, and bridges at lines 78, 89, 102, 113, 130, 148, 156.
findings.fix: Add the set-level analogues needed by the existing contour API: at least uniqueness/value recovery if a `cauchyPV` value is introduced, plus `congr_along_curve`, `zero`, `const_mul`, `add`, `sum`, and existence-level forms where applicable.
findings.issue: `HasCauchyPV` exposes only `hasCauchyPV_iff` and `.intro`; unlike `HasCauchyPVAt`, it has no named value/uniqueness or operation API, so consumers cannot use the set-level PV as a characterized value-bearing interface.

summary: The new public predicate is exposed as the roadmap-level principal-value interface, but its characteristic API is too thin for downstream use without unfolding or re-proving the pointwise API patterns.
